stem: What is the human's role in loop engineering?
choices: Dictate every step to the AI agent
Define the goal and workflow
Let the agent decide its own stop condition
Write the agent's code line by line
explanation: The human sets the goal and the shape of the workflow, and the agent carries out the steps inside that loop. Dictating every step is the opposite of loop engineering.

stem: Select all the responsibilities that belong to the human in loop engineering. Select all that apply.
choices: Define the goal and workflow
Dictate every step to the agent
Set the evaluation criteria
Decide the stop condition
explanation: The human owns the goal, the criteria that say whether output is good, and the rule for when to stop. Dictating each step removes the loop itself and is not a human responsibility in this model.

stem: In loop engineering, what is an agent loop?
choices: One prompt and one answer, then the session ends
A fixed script that never checks its own results
Planning, acting, observing the result, and checking it, repeated until a stop condition
Training the model again on its own output
explanation: The loop is the repeated cycle of plan, act, observe and check, which continues until a stop rule fires. A single prompt is not a loop, and a script without checks cannot correct itself.

choices: The point where the model's weights are saved to disk
The token limit of a single reply
The rule that ends the loop, such as all tests passing or a maximum number of rounds
The moment the user closes the browser
explanation: A stop condition is a rule the loop checks, so it ends when the goal is met or when a limit is reached. Without one, the loop may never end.

stem: Good loop engineering dictates every step to the agent so that it cannot go off track.
choices: True
False
explanation: Dictating every step gives up the benefit of the loop. Good practice is to set the goal, the checks and the stop rule, and let the agent choose its steps within them.

stem: Why define evaluation criteria before the loop starts?
choices: So the agent and the human share a definition of when the output counts as done and correct
So the model uses fewer tokens
So the model trains faster
So the agent can skip the stop condition
explanation: Without criteria fixed in advance, the agent can declare its own work finished. The criteria give the check something to test against.

stem: Which stop condition is the safest?
choices: Run until the agent says it is finished
Stop after one step
Stop when all tests pass or after a set number of rounds, whichever comes first
Never stop; the human will intervene
explanation: Combining a success test with a hard limit prevents both early stopping and endless loops. Trusting the agent's own claim of completion skips the external check.

stem: Select all that are good practice in loop engineering. Select all that apply.
choices: Set a maximum number of iterations
Log each step so a human can review what the agent did
Let the agent grade its own work with no external check
Define success criteria before the loop starts
Leave out the stop condition to save time
explanation: Limits, logs and criteria defined up front are the core controls of a loop. Self-grading with no external check and having no stop condition are the failure modes the discipline exists to prevent.

stem: How does loop engineering differ from prompt engineering?
choices: Loop engineering designs the repeated cycle around the model, while prompt engineering shapes a single request
Loop engineering trains new models, while prompt engineering writes single requests
Loop engineering chooses file formats, while prompt engineering chooses colours
There is no difference; they are two names for one practice
explanation: A prompt shapes one request. A loop designs the cycle of many steps, checks and stops around one or more model calls.

stem: An agent keeps editing a file and then undoing its own edits. Which fix is closest to loop engineering?
choices: Raise the temperature so it tries new things
Remove every tool the agent has
Add an observe step that compares the result with the goal, plus a stop rule
Make the initial prompt longer
explanation: The fix is structural: the loop needs to observe the result against the goal and stop or change course. Adjusting randomness or length treats the symptom, not the loop.

stem: What is the name for a stop rule that ends an agent loop after a fixed number of rounds?
explanation: A maximum-iterations limit, sometimes called an iteration cap. It is a safety stop that works alongside a success test.

stem: Who sets the goal and the evaluation criteria in loop engineering?
choices: The agent itself
The human
The vector store
The model provider, automatically
explanation: The human sets the goal and criteria, because the agent cannot be the judge of its own success. The other options are not roles in the loop.
